one_month_reasoning: Nov 1 2026 is a Sunday, so the mark is the Fri Oct 30 close. Avnet's own FQ1 FY27 report most likely falls outside the window. I checked the supervisor's finding on EDGAR: every fiscal Q1-Q3 earnings 8-K (Item 2.02) came exactly 32 days after the Saturday quarter-end (Oct 30 2024, Oct 29 2025, Jan 28 2026, Apr 29 2026). Q1 FY27 ends Oct 3, which points to Wed Nov 4. I put about 10% on the print landing by Oct 30. Arrow also falls outside: its Q2 2026 quarter ended Jul 4 and it reported Aug 6 (33 days), so Q3 should come about Nov 5. What does fall inside the window is industry read-through. TI reports Q3 around Oct 20-27 (MarketBeat estimate Oct 27) after guiding $5.7-6.2B against a $5.5B consensus. STMicro and NXP report in late October. The early-October ECIA Pulse comes out too; its September outlook was flat at about 135, with Q3 end-market sentiment projected down to 130.8 and respondents expecting cooling into Q4. Weekly memory spot prices are mixed (TrendForce Sep 23: DDR4 is correcting, DDR5 varies by part). These pull in both directions: strong supplier prints against fading sentiment. I have no directional edge, so I centre the distribution on today's price. The shape is a lognormal mixture, 90% at a 10.2% monthly sigma (37%/3.5 is about 10.6%) and 10% at a 15% sigma. The wide component covers a possible in-window print, a peer guide shock, and post-+105% momentum or reversal risk.

fair_value.method: Weighted blend of three methods, about $95. Forward P/E: $10.9 NTM EPS (Oct-2027) x 9x = $98, weight 50%. EV/EBIT: FY27E $36B sales x 4.2% adjusted operating margin x 7.5x, less ~$3.35B forward net debt ($3.06B reported), on ~86M diluted shares = $93, weight 30%. Mid-cycle: $7.5 EPS x 12x = $90, weight 20%.

methods.name: P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: Starts from the $2.85 Q1 run-rate (~$11.4/yr). Arrow's backlog into 1H27 and WSTS's +27% 2027 forecast support a plateau through mid-2027. ECIA sentiment has fallen from its June peak of 154.1 to 136.7 in August, with Q3 end-markets projected at 130.8 and cooling expected into Q4, so I shade FY28 quarters below the run-rate (~$11.0). I then cut about 1% for net convert dilution: ~86M diluted at $107 versus the 85M in guidance.

At the FY23 peak (adjusted EPS $8.06) AVT traded at about 6x; today it trades at about 10x consensus and 9.4x the run-rate. The gap from 6x to 10x means the market is already pricing roughly a 40% smaller fall in earnings than a 2023-style unwind would imply. My industry evidence shows the cycle cooling, not breaking: sentiment is falling, but lead times and supplier price increases still hold. That justifies giving back about one turn of multiple over 12 months, not four.

bear.story: The shortage unwinds 2022-23 style. Customer safety stock and forecast buffering (Lattice asking for a full year's buffer, hyperscaler HDD hoarding) reverse in mid-2027. ECIA sentiment keeps sliding below 120, book-to-bill falls below 1, and pricing tailwinds fade. The market looks through ~$10 EPS to a FY28 decline, and the multiple compresses to about 6x, the prior-peak level.

base.story: Tightness persists through most of 2027 (WSTS +27%, Arrow backlog into 1H27, supplier price increases sticking), and EPS plateaus at about $11 annualized. Sentiment keeps cooling from its June peak, and the multiple drifts from 10x to about 9x as investors price the cycle peak. The stock ends roughly flat to slightly down.

bull.story: Analog, MCU and FPGA allocation lasts into 2028, and supplier price increases flow through as distributor margin. EC margin moves above 4.5%, NTM EPS reaches about $14, and the stock holds about 10x.

thesis_break_reason: A level near $68 (about -36%, about 6.2x the $10.9 NTM EPS and 6x the $11.4 run-rate) would mean the market sees the cycle as past its peak. That would show up as book-to-bill below 1 at Avnet or Arrow, an outright sequential guide-down at the Nov 4 or Jan print, or a broad lead-time collapse in the Greensheet or ECIA data. That is the 2023 pattern, not ordinary 37%-vol noise. The supervisor centres the agents' range at $70. I keep $68 because on my slightly lower ~$10.9 EPS the prior-peak 6x multiple lands nearer $66-68.

reasoning: Avnet is a broadline components distributor in a strong upcycle. Q4 FY26 sales were $8.3B (+48% YoY) with adjusted EPS of $2.28. The Q1 guide of $2.85 implies about $11.4 annualized EPS, about 9.4x at $106.94; consensus of ~$10.5 lags the guide. The value chain confirms the upcycle. Arrow components sales are +39% with book-to-bill above 1 and backlog into 1H27. Analog lead times are 60-70 weeks, and Microchip, ADI and TI raised prices from Aug to Oct. TI guided Q3 to $5.7-6.2B against a $5.5B consensus, and WSTS sees +27% in 2027. Late-cycle signals are building. ECIA sentiment went from 154.1 in June to 136.7 in August, with a flat September outlook and Q3 end-markets projected at 130.8. Memory spot prices are mixed to soft, and customers are buffering a year of forecast. Round-2 changes after the supervisor's review: I confirmed on EDGAR that the next print is ~Nov 4 (32-day cadence) and Arrow's is ~Nov 5, both after the 1-month mark, so I dropped the earnings-gap widening from the 1-month ladder. I now label net debt as $3.06B reported and ~$3.35B forward (estimate), use ~86M diluted shares for the convert, and trim NTM EPS to $10.9. Fair value is now $95 (was $96). On the supervisor's question of how much late-cycle risk 10x already prices: the market has gone 4 turns above the 6x peak multiple, so it assumes no full unwind. My evidence shows cooling, not breaking, which is why I use 9x and not 6x. The 12-month ladder is a mixture: 75% lognormal (median $101, sigma 0.37) and 25% wide bear-skewed (median $92, sigma 0.55). That gives a median of about $99-100, P(>=107) = 0.44 and a scenario mean of about $103. It is a touch more bearish than round 1 because sentiment cooling is now projected through Q4. Research in round 2 was about 6 queries: EDGAR submissions for Avnet and Arrow, ECIA, TI guidance, and TrendForce memory spot prices.
